body: **2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** (a password painted masked; the shot one more reader of bounds) — made the password mask a blitz-paint change for every document and renderer (bullets via `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input`), and stated that a `screenshot` reads only the model's bounds and changes nothing (no focus move, `has_changes` false, next diff empty). Why it matters: the precedent for a blitz-paint engine change ratified per change for every document (as F1 is). It also binds rows `decision/password-never-revealed`, `decision/password-value-masked` and `decision/screenshot-changes-nothing`, which the canvas paint fix and the new canvas-text checks must leave green in both layout modes.

**2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep** (the password click caret measured) — measured the password click caret at index 5 vs 2, real glyph widths reaching it, and routed the fix to a residual. Why it matters: it is the history of row `decision/password-caret-by-bullets`. The chunk now hands the document's font context to widgets, and that must not change how a password field's caret or bullets are shaped.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** (the toggle per role and the snapshot's sources, plus `inert` and `disabled` in focus order, keys and the hit, later ratified at the Epoch 2 close) — changed three readings. A truthy `inert` takes focusability, hits and the tree away, and a hit passes through it. Disabled-ness is keyed by `is_disabled` for the pointer, click, activation and focus gates. A disabled form control stops the click walk. The password caret is placed by bullets. Why it matters: these are rows `decision/inert-subtree-excluded`, `decision/inert-element-takes-no-hit`, `contract/hit-testing/inert`, `decision/disabled-control-stops-click-walk` and `decision/password-caret-by-bullets`. Re-framing a custom widget's pointer events in `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs` must not bypass the inert hit skip or the disabled gates.

**2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock** — added that two pointer clicks on one point within 500 ms and 2 px are a double click, read on the document's clock (the harness's `VirtualClock` on a harness document), each click still focusing its target. Ratified at the Epoch 2 close. Why it matters: rows `decision/double-click-on-document-clock` and `decision/double-click-threshold`. The point used for the double click is the hit point, and that must stay unmoved when a widget's event coordinates move into its content-box frame.

**2026-10-13-range-input-interaction** — made a click focus a range input without moving its value. A main-button pointerdown sets the value by position, from the hit's fraction of the content box. Why it matters: rows `decision/range-pointerdown-sets-value`, `contract/range-input/main-button-pointerdown`, `decision/range-click-focuses-not-value` and `contract/range-input/click`. This is an existing engine reading of pointer coordinates in a content-box frame. The new mapping of widget pointer events (border-box origin plus border and padding) must agree with it and must not move the range arm.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** (Enter and Space activate, a click focuses a button; `disabled` by presence) — changed three things, in every document. A pointer click on a button or a submit/reset/button input focuses it, and a submit button then submits its form owner. Enter and Space dispatch a synthetic Click. Disabled-ness is keyed one way, by presence (founder «По наличию»). Why it matters: rows `decision/click-focuses-buttons`, `decision/synthetic-click-at-node-centre` and `decision/disabled-by-attribute-presence`. The synthetic click lands at the node's centre, which a widget event-frame change must not re-map.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (a non-invertible transform takes no hit) — added that a transform whose determinant is 0 or not finite answers `None` from `Node::hit_inner` for its whole subtree, asserted by `hit_non_invertible_transform` in both layout modes. Why it matters: this is the only prior a11y-plan ruling on hits under a CSS transform. The chunk moves a widget's paint inside the element's transform (`M · T(content origin)`) and keeps transforms unapplied to the widget's event coordinates, so the hit path and the widget's event frame must stay consistent with it.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (`change` on a checkbox and a radio; a `multiple` select's keys and row clicks; the driver on a `multiple` select) — the checkbox and radio arms of `handle_click` now dispatch one engine `change` after `input`. A `multiple` select now takes its own keys and row clicks (`click_select_row`). The driver's `type` on a `multiple` select now focuses it with no click. Why it matters: rows `decision/one-engine-change-per-checkable-click`, `decision/checkable-click-toggles-and-focuses`, `contract/multiple-select/keys-and-row-clicks` and `decision/driver-type-focuses-select-no-click`. These are pointer paths in the same `handle_dom_event` / `handle_click` dispatch the chunk edits for the `custom-widget` arm.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the select list as a scope entity; what opens it; a click, the pointer and focus on an open list) — made the single select's list an engine overlay on every document, with one `select_list` field. `hit_with_scrollbar` answers it first and `paint_scene` paints it after the root's render. A click opens or closes it. A label's click focuses the select and opens nothing. Why it matters: rows `decision/single-select-engine-overlay-list` and `decision/label-click-focuses-select-only`. This is the precedent for a blitz-paint paint-order and hit-order change for every document. The widget's scene, now placed inside the element's transform, must still paint under the overlay list, and the list must still be hit first.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (an open list against `:open`, clips and `opacity`) — the list paints whole past an `opacity` ancestor and a box that clips its select. A point the list does not cover reads what paint shows. A driver `click` on an element under the list is refused `covered`. Why it matters: rows `contract/driver-click-refusals/covered` and `decision/single-select-engine-overlay-list`. This entry ruled clipping for the list. F1 ruled against clipping a widget's scene (option B not taken), and that left-unclipped scene must not break the `covered` refusal or the hit-follows-paint reading.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (how an open list's labels leave) — ruled that a page's option and group labels leave an open list only as painted pixels in a `screenshot` and the snapshot's `name`, with no log site. Ratified by the founder (F7/F1 and Q1). Why it matters: this is the a11y-plan precedent for page-authored text crossing as shot pixels. The chunk's canvas text leaves the same way, settled as inside the ratified crossing (F3), with no log site and no snapshot field added.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the served pages, the lint's option overlap and the scrollbar's band; the flight booker's select) — added two readings. Right after a `scroll`, a main-button pointerdown in the shown overlay scrollbar's band is a thumb drag that dispatches nothing, so a driver `click` there needs an `advance` past the fade. A driver `click` on a flight-type option is refused `covered`. Why it matters: rows `decision/driver-click-in-shown-scrollbar-drags` and `contract/driver-click-refusals/covered`. These are pointer-hit precedents that a widget's pointer-event remap must leave intact.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — built detection of the driver's `disabled` refusal on the snapshot's `enabled` reading alone. `Session::run` refuses a `click` or `type` when `enabled` is `Some(false)`, the first screen-level check, with nothing dispatched and focus unmoved. Why it matters: rows `contract/driver-actions/disabled` and `contract/driver-refusal/disabled`. The scope adds no new verb, cause or refusal, and these readings must stay as they are.

**2026-10-20-select-by-id** — added that a click focuses a select but no option is clicked, and that a label's click reaches its bound labelable element. Why it matters: these are the roots of rows `decision/label-click-focuses-select-only` and `decision/driver-type-focuses-select-no-click`, which belong to the click-dispatch area the chunk's `events/mod.rs` change sits in.

**2026-11-21-single-select-sized-as-a-list-box** (1. A11y Scope Summary and 5. Keyboard Navigation) — changed `decision/single-select-engine-overlay-list` so that only a drop-down select (display size 1) opens the overlay list and a single list box opens none. Added `contract/single-list-box/row-click` and `contract/single-list-box/keys`. Why it matters: these are the latest wordings of two picked rows. They are the current engine overlay and row-click contracts in the paint and hit paths this chunk edits.

**2026-11-13-upstream-sync-determinism-and-exploration** (5. Keyboard Navigation) — added row `decision/hidden-checkable-label-toggle`: a native checkbox or radio keeps its checked state with no box, so a label click toggles it even under `display: none`. Ratified as upstream's behaviour. Why it matters: this is a picked row, guarded by `clicking_label_toggles_hidden_checkbox`, on the label-click path of the same dispatch.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the one actionable rule and the check's listener leg) — made `unkeyed_actionable` and `actionable_nodes` share one crate-private `Readings` rule: focusable, an interactive role, or exact current listeners other than `mounted`. The `data-dioxus-id` mark now serves event dispatch alone. Why it matters: row `decision/one-actionable-rule`. A canvas widget element (`<object>` with `custom-widget`) on the stand is read by this one rule. The chunk's dispatch change must not add a second actionable mapping.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (citations re-pointed after the take; blending paints with no frame test) — re-pointed the a11y-plan citations into `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs`, `document.rs` and blitz-paint's `render.rs`, the files this chunk edits. It also recorded that `render_element` pushes viewport-wide blend layers, that the open list paints last past them, and that no test paints a blended element to a frame. Why it matters: citations into `custom_widget.rs`, `document.rs` and `render.rs` move when the chunk edits them and are owed a re-point. The paint order the widget's new transform-composed append joins is the order recorded here.

**2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts** (6. Visual Design Verification: 2 and 3 rows) — made two paint and text changes on the open list. A row now takes the tallest row's line height, so a larger authored font is painted whole. The highlight pair equals the default sheet's chosen-row pair. Why it matters: this is the most recent engine-paint change to the overlay in row `decision/single-select-engine-overlay-list`. It shows that text the engine paints outside the DOM text path is re-pinned by a painted witness in both layout modes, as the chunk's canvas «Hg» check must be.

Moves a custom widget's forwarded pointer events (move, down, up, cancel, leave) into the same content-box frame, the border-box origin plus left/top border and padding in CSS px, still with no transform applied; a sub-document's events keep the border-box origin.
Lets canvas text draw from the bundled fonts through the document's own font context: a new defaulted method on the widget trait hands each widget that context before it paints, and the document gains a public accessor of its font context, both behind the custom-widget feature.
Every new check is run red first (before its fix or with the fix reverted) and its red reading kept beside its green, in both layout modes; the existing canvas shot and widget layout checks are re-read green, and the stand's served tasks' readings stand.

body: A custom widget's paint size becomes its content-box size and its scene is placed at the content-box origin inside the element's transform, in both layout modes; read on the stand with padding, a border and a scale transform.

A custom widget's pointer events (PointerMove, PointerDown, PointerUp, PointerCancel, PointerLeave) carry coordinates relative to its content-box origin in CSS px, no transform applied; a sub-document's events stay at the border-box origin. Rows on pointer event delivery, hit-testing and pointer coordinate frames bind it.
No clip to the content box is added: a widget's scene stays unclipped, as today, unlike a replaced image.

Canvas text is shaped from the document's own font context, the same bundled set the document's text reads, so canvas text on the stand reads the same font in both layout modes; no font file or asset enters the tree.

Two new public items behind custom-widget (a defaulted Widget trait method and a document font context accessor), each with a doc comment, diverging from upstream and flagged upstreamable; no implementor changes.
Canvas text leaves only as pixels in a screenshot, inside the ratified canvas crossing; it gains no other crossing.

The screenshot's contract stands: an 800 x 600 shot over opaque white, byte-identical across processes on one host, fonts-unavailable before anything is painted, a password input painted masked, and a shot changes nothing and runs no step.
The stand's served tasks keep their snapshot, lint and actions readings, and the committed kept checks and stand checks keep theirs unless a ruling moves one, then re-recorded, never loosened.
Every new check is run red first and its red reading kept in evidence beside its green, every kept log path respelled with no temp or home path.
Every new check runs in both layout modes, incremental and non-incremental.
No new verb, argument, carrier, cause, session error, exit, log field or span; no content in a log field.
Every build, test and CI cargo leg passes --locked; parley enters only as a dev-dependency already in the lock, no package enters it; the doc leg joins the local gate for the new public items.
The last wrap's CI verdict, still in progress, is re-read before this chunk's push and never folded as green.

body: The Widget trait's paint receives the widget's content-box size times scale, not its border-box size; with padding, a border or neither, what a widget paints covers its content box exactly.

Pointer events forwarded to a custom widget (pointer move, down, up, cancel and leave, the variants mapped to a UiEvent) carry coordinates relative to the widget's content-box origin: the node's absolute position plus its left and top border and padding, in CSS px; a transform stays unapplied, and events forwarded to a sub-document keep the border-box origin.

body: A custom widget's paint is handed its content-box size times scale, not its border-box size, with padding and border alike.

A custom widget's scene is appended at its content-box origin inside the element's own transform (M then T of the content origin), so under a CSS transform it lands where the transform puts the content box.
A custom widget's scene stays unclipped, as today: no layer and no content-box clip is pushed for it (F1 option B not taken).

Pointer events forwarded to a custom widget (move, down, up, cancel, leave) carry coordinates relative to its content-box origin, the border-box origin plus left and top border and padding in CSS px; no transform is applied to them, and a sub-document's events keep the border-box origin.
The Widget trait gains one defaulted method through which blitz-paint hands each widget the document's font context before its paint, behind the custom-widget feature; no implementor changes.

BaseDocument gains a public accessor of its font context, behind the custom-widget feature; each new public item carries its doc comment, is flagged upstreamable, and the doc leg joins the local gate.

Canvas text is shaped from the bundled fonts through the document's own font context, so a widget's text on the stand reads the same font as the document's text; no font file or other asset enters the tree.
Canvas text leaves a shot as pixels, inside the ratified crossing of canvas content as shot pixels; nothing of it crosses as text or data.
An app paints the canvas from Rust through the widget's paint returning a scene; no web Canvas 2D context for page scripts and no wgpu canvas.

body: A custom widget's paint receives its content-box size times the scale, not its border-box size; a widget with padding and a border reads its content box (100 by 60 where it read 130 by 90).

A custom widget's scene is placed at its content-box origin inside the element's own transform, so under a scale transform its content offset is scaled with it, and nothing it paints falls outside its border box.
A custom widget's scene stays unclipped, as today; no content-box clip is pushed for it, unlike a replaced image.

Pointer move, down, up, cancel and leave events forwarded to a custom widget carry coordinates relative to its content-box origin in CSS px, the frame its paint draws in; no transform is applied to them, and a sub-document's events keep the border-box origin.
Canvas text is shaped from the document's own font context, handed to each widget before its paint; a widget that draws text paints the same bundled font as the document's text, in both layout modes.

Every new stand check runs in both layout modes, incremental and non-incremental, and reads the same.
